gloss: to become moss-covered; to grow mossy

definitions.gloss: to become moss-covered; to grow mossy
definitions.explanation: For stones, ground, buildings, or other surfaces to become covered with moss over time. Often used poetically to evoke age, tranquility, and the passage of time.

examples.english: The stones in the garden are covered in moss.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{石段|いしだん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{苔|こけ}むして⟦{滑|すべ}りやすく→滑りやすい：27611_suberiyasui⟧⟦なっている→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The old stone steps have become mossy and slippery.

examples.japanese: {何百年|なんびゃくねん}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{経|た}った→経つ：09892_tatsu⟧⟦{石垣|いしがき}→石垣：19673_ishigaki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{苔|こけ}むして、⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{重|おも}み→重み：14503_omomi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じさせる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: The stone wall, hundreds of years old, is covered in moss, giving a sense of the weight of history.

notes:
A poetic and literary verb evoking the passage of time and natural beauty. Famous from the Japanese national anthem {君|きみ}が{代|よ}: "⟦{苔|こけ}→苔：04991_koke⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧むす⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧" (until the pebbles grow into moss-covered boulders).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苔|こけ}むした⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧: a moss-covered stone
- {苔|こけ}むした⟦{屋根|やね}→屋根：02264_yane⟧: a mossy roof
- {苔|こけ}むす⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧: until moss grows (i.e., for an eternity)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Moss holds special aesthetic value in Japanese culture, symbolizing age, tranquility, and wabi-sabi. ⟦{苔|こけ}→苔：04991_koke⟧{寺|でら} (Saihoji temple in Kyoto) is famous for its moss garden.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb (す row). Conjugates: {苔|こけ}むさない, {苔|こけ}むして, {苔|こけ}むします. The past participle {苔|こけ}むした is commonly used as a modifier.
